page: Microsoft Azure HX176-24rs is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the HX family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel processors. The server is equipped with a massive memory allocation of 1408.0 GB, which translates to 58.67 GB of RAM per core.

For local storage, the HX176-24rs includes a bundled 4332 GB NVMe SSD. It is also Premium Storage capable and supports Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) networking capabilities, which facilitates high-throughput, low-latency communication between nodes. There are no integrated GPUs on this instance.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local NVMe storage, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for applications requiring massive memory footprints relative to compute cores, avoiding the need to over-provision vCPUs just to acquire sufficient RAM. The hardware profile is suited for large-scale databases, in-memory analytics, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-intensive scientific computing workloads.
